cases.question: How do I do the start-of-shift check on a powered pallet truck?

judge.reason: All key facts are present and match SOP-EQ-01 Sections 3–5, including the powered-only checks and correct out-of-use steps; nothing invented or unsafe.

answer.answer: Check the truck at the start of each shift and record it on the Pre-Use Equipment Checklist (SOP-EQ-01, Pallets & Handling Equipment). A powered pallet truck needs the standard pallet truck checks plus the powered-only checks. Only operators trained and signed off on the truck may use it unsupervised.
steps: Check the forks are straight, with no cracks or bends.
Check the wheels and fork rollers are present, undamaged and turn freely.
Check the truck lifts, holds a load without sinking, and lowers when released.
Check the handle and controls work and return to neutral.
Check the battery is charged and the charging lead is undamaged.
Check the brakes, horn and emergency reverse (belly button) work.
Record the check on the Pre-Use Equipment Checklist (paper or handheld).
If any check fails: stop using the truck, park it with forks fully lowered and clear of aisles, fire exits and emergency lanes, switch it off and remove the key.
Tag it 'Do Not Use — Faulty' with the fault, date and who found it. Do not attempt a repair.
Tell your FLM straight away and log the fault in the incident system the same shift.

cases.question: A delivery is 8 units short on an order of 200. Is that a large discrepancy?

judge.reason: Fully correct: the answer applies both thresholds (4% and under 10 units) and requires logging within 15 minutes. It holds the pallet in staging pending FLM confirmation and correctly limits Senior FLM escalation to high-value or repeated discrepancies.

answer.answer: No. 8 units short on an order of 200 is not a large discrepancy. A large discrepancy is more than 5% of the expected quantity, or more than 10 units (either one is enough). 5% of 200 is 10 units, and 8 is both under 10 units and under 5% (4%). It is still a discrepancy, so it must be logged and handled under goods-in discrepancy rules.
steps: Do not guess or accept it as correct: log the shortage as a discrepancy in the incident system (or paper log if the system is down) within 15 minutes of discovery.
Hold the rest of the affected pallet in goods-in staging. Do not put away stock with an open discrepancy until your FLM confirms how to proceed.
Tell your FLM. If the item is high-value (unit value over £500) or the discrepancies are repeated, the FLM escalates to the Senior FLM.
If your FLM is unavailable, go to the Senior FLM.
